title: A calcium–albumin spline surface worsened frozen grip-strength prediction in a reused NHANES cross-cohort audit
abstract: We tested whether calcium-by-albumin spline products improve concurrent combined-handgrip prediction beyond total calcium, albumin, conventional corrected calcium and body-size/renal covariates. Models trained in NHANES2011–2012 (n=4011) were frozen for separately recruited2013–2014 participants (n=4505). Adding25 terms increased examination-weighted mean squared error from 133.389 to 135.132 kg². The registered improvement criterion failed. Joint bootstrap refits were numerically unstable, with a95% delta interval [0.436,1954.283] kg²; a post-primary scale-floor challenge is reported, not substituted. This negative reused-data audit establishes neither physiological absence nor clinical harm. Validation in a separate independent study remains incomplete.
